hero.headline: Treasure Coast Traffic Report: Major Ramp and Road Closures Planned July 12-17
hero.teaser:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

Driv
hero.body:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

Drivers across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 10-17 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department of Transportation's latest weekly traffic report identifies multiple lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties. FDOT placed additional emphasis on full road, ramp and bridge closures expected to have the greatest effect on motorists.

## Major closures to know about

### I-95 exit to Bridge Road closing overnight in Martin County

The southbound Interstate 95 exit ramp to County Road 708, also known as Bridge Road, at Exit 96 will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16.**

Drivers will be directed to exit at Kanner Highway, travel south on Pratt Whitney Road and then head east on Bridge Road.

The closure is needed for roadway construction. Weather-related contingency dates are scheduled for July 19-23.

### Port St. Lucie neighborhood roads could close for several days

Extended closures are planned along several side streets near the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project.

Closures may begin at **7 a.m. Monday, July 13, and continue until 5 p.m. Friday, July 17,** on portions of SW Jaslo Avenue, SW Jacoby Avenue, SW McCullough Avenue, SW McCall Road and SW McHord Avenue.

The roads will close intermittently for drainage and utility installation. FDOT said adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained.

Detours will generally use SW Paar Drive, SW McCain Street, SW McIntyre Street, SW Kabane Street and other nearby roads, depending on the closure location.

### I-95 ramp to Orange Avenue closing in Fort Pierce

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to westbound State Road 68, or Orange Avenue, will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16.**

Motorists will be detoured using the exit to eastbound Orange Avenue, northbound Jenkins Road and westbound Loop Road before returning to westbound Orange Avenue.

The work includes paving and lighting installation. Contingency dates are July 19-23.

## Martin County traffic impacts

Motorists should expect overnight lane closures on I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line. Up to two lanes may close in each direction during overnight hours for milling, resurfacing and signage work.

On U.S. 1 in Stuart, two lanes may close intermittently between Fischer Street and Decker Avenue from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday for sign installation.

A1A between Shore Village Terrace and the Jensen Beach Causeway may be reduced to one lane at times from Monday through Friday for drainage work and pavement widening. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic through the work zone.

Martin Highway between Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard may also have intermittent overnight lane closures Tuesday through Thursday.

FDOT is additionally warning drivers in advance about several upcoming I-95 ramp closures at Martin Highway and Kanner Highway later in July and early August.

## St. Lucie County traffic impacts

Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Seafury Lane and Lennard Road may have daytime lane closures Monday through Friday. Two lanes may close overnight from Sunday through Friday for drainage work, milling and repaving.

U.S. 1 between Jennings Road and Golden Oak Trail may also have lane restrictions during both daytime and overnight hours.

On SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard, one lane may close between Jordin Avenue and Alcantarra Boulevard from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday as crews continue the widening project.

Up to two lanes may close overnight on I-95 between Glades Cut-Off Road and the area just south of Okeechobee Road for milling and repaving.

Midway Road between Florida's Turnpike and Selvitz Road may continue to have intermittent weekday lane closures through September as part of the roadway widening project.

## North Causeway marine restrictions

The new A1A North Causeway Bridge remains open to vehicle traffic, but significant restrictions are planned for boaters using the Intracoastal Waterway.

The existing drawbridge will not open to marine traffic from 7 a.m. Thursday, July 16, through 6 p.m. Saturday, July 18. Boats capable of passing beneath the bridge without an opening may continue through.

Additional single-leaf openings, partial channel obstructions and temporary full channel closures are scheduled through July 24 as crews remove portions of the former drawbridge.

FDOT said the marine work will not affect vehicle traffic on the new bridge.

## Indian River County traffic impacts

One lane may remain closed on the 17th Street bridges between Indian River Boulevard and Indian Bay Drive as bridge rehabilitation continues.

At the new I-95 interchange at Oslo Road, one or two interstate lanes may close overnight Sunday through Thursday for bridge work, milling and resurfacing.

On 90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street, one lane may close overnight Sunday through Friday for construction associated with the 85th Street widening project.

Drivers traveling near Sebastian Inlet should also expect intermittent lane or shoulder closures on A1A through Friday, July 17. Flaggers will direct motorists through the work zone.

Sections of the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park will remain closed during construction of the new bridge. The closures are expected to continue through spring 2032, although the park and portions of both parking lots remain open.

## Plan ahead

Construction schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions. Motorists should allow additional travel time, follow posted detours and use caution around workers and equipment.

Real-time interstate traffic conditions are available through Florida 511. Updated lane closure information is also available through FDOT District Four.

cards.headline: 24 immigration arrests conducted in Martin County this week
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Law Enforcement conducted 24 immigration arrests in Martin County on Tuesday, according to data kept by the agency. The Martin County Sheriff's Office confirms FDLE was the agency behind the arrests. WPTV has reached out to ICE and FDLE for comment.

South Florida immigration attorneys are noticing a shift in how federal and local law enforcement are carrying out immigration arrests, with fewer high-profile raids that spark public outrage and raise legal concerns. Renata Castro, an immigration attorney based in Coral Springs, said she has seen the shift firsthand. She said she is seeing more detained cases and traffic-related detentions that result in immigration detention. The change appears to coincide with Markwayne Mullin replacing Kristi Noem as Homeland Security Secretary in March. Castro said the approach under Noem was markedly different, with many arrests without a warrant and "a big spectacle overall." Immigration attorneys previously questioned the legality of many detentions carried out during Noem's tenure. Castro said she does not have those same questions about the current approach, noting these are arrests without warrants but still following safeguards that local law enforcement must abide by. According to NBC News, ICE arrested 10,000 people over five days this month.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie 6,000-seat soccer stadium groundbreaking set for November, new renderings released
cards.body:
Professional soccer is still set to begin next year in Port St. Lucie, with the club releasing new renderings this week of its 6,000-seat stadium. Representatives for Port St. Lucie SC announced Friday that groundbreaking is anticipated later this year, with current plans targeting November. The stadium will be built at the Walton & One development, a 46-acre mixed-use redevelopment project located along U.S. 1 and Walton Road. While the club's inaugural season begins in 2027, the future stadium is scheduled to open in early 2028. The team has not announced where they plan to play next year while the facility is under construction. The club posted Thursday on social media that their home venue will be a place where soccer, community, and unforgettable moments will come together. The team said every space has been designed to create unforgettable experiences, from matchdays to concerts, festivals, and community events, calling it a destination built for everyone. The 6,000-seat venue will have the flexibility to grow in capacity and will serve as a year-round gathering place.

Port St. Lucie resident Zach Woods said he thinks there's nothing to do in PSL for the most part and this may be the first cool thing that we've ever actually brought here. However, Woods said you can't really even get out here on US-1 before this and it's a nightmare, so he thinks the additional traffic on gamedays will be huge. Focus Sanders, a barber at Sapp's Barbershop, said the venue offers more business because it's going to bring more people over here, including people coming from maybe out of town who didn't get a haircut. Sanders said he's not liking the traffic that's going to come, but he is liking the business traffic. Ticket deposits are currently available online. It was announced last October that the city had been awarded a United Soccer League League One Team, with city council members unanimously approving both the funding and operating agreements. The city said the stadium is an $80 million economic investment, and no taxpayer money will be used for its construction.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce teen named Southeast Region Youth of the Year wins trip to FIFA World Cup finals
cards.body:
Enrique Rosario Liz, a St. Lucie teenager named Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, was surprised Friday at the Boys & Girls Club of St. Lucie County in Fort Pierce with a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. He will serve as one of 12 club members from across the country selected to be an official Coca-Cola flag bearer at the FIFA World Cup finals on July 19. The surprise came courtesy of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America and their partnership with the Coca-Cola Company. Rosario Liz had already been juggling a packed summer, preparing for move-in at the University of Florida and an internship, but said the World Cup had been on his mind. When the box containing the news was walked into the room surrounded by fellow club members, his reaction was immediate. Along with the trip, Rosario Liz also received official gear inside the box.

Rosario Liz credited the Boys & Girls Club with shaping who he has become as a leader. The club really helped him to find what his leadership style was going to be and really redefined what his definition of leadership was, he said. Rosario Liz closed with a message for the younger members of the club looking up to him, telling them to please stay with their Boys & Girls Clubs because one day he wants to see each and every one of them in the same position that he is in right now.

cards.headline: Indian River County schools work to reverse enrollment declines amid school choice expansion
cards.body:
New research examines how the Indian River County school district is working to reverse enrollment declines amid expanding school choice options in Florida. The case study highlights the district's strategy as families have more alternatives to traditional public schools.

The research comes as school districts across Florida face increased competition from charter schools, private school voucher programs, and other educational alternatives. Indian River County has experienced enrollment declines in recent years as the state has expanded school choice legislation.

The case study explores specific approaches the district is implementing to retain and attract students. School choice expansion in Florida has accelerated in recent years, giving families increased options for where to send their children.

The research provides insight into how one Treasure Coast district is adapting to the changing educational landscape. Indian River County school officials are developing strategies to compete in an environment where families have unprecedented choices for their children's education.

hero.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse offers 165 years of history with panoramic views
hero.teaser: Built in 1860, the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse has guided ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years. The 105-step climb to the top rewards visitors with breathtaking views of the Atlantic Ocean, Jupiter Inlet, and Loxahatchee and Indian rivers.
hero.body:
The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse stands as a striking red brick tower rising high above the inlet. Built in 1860, the lighthouse has guided countless ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years. The historic landmark continues to draw visitors who want to experience both its rich history and the spectacular views from the top.

The 105-step climb to the top follows a narrow spiral staircase that lighthouse keepers once climbed night after night to keep the powerful Fresnel lens shining for mariners. The journey upward offers a glimpse into the daily routine of those who maintained this vital navigational aid through the decades. Each step carries the weight of history, connecting modern visitors to the keepers who dedicated their lives to guiding ships safely along Florida's treacherous coastline.

Reaching the gallery at the top rewards visitors with breathtaking panoramic views in every direction. The Atlantic Ocean stretches endlessly to the east, while the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet meet the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers below. Boats glide through the channel as the sea breeze sweeps across the observation deck, making even warm Florida mornings feel comfortable. The vantage point provides a unique perspective on the surrounding waterways and coastline that mariners have relied upon for over a century and a half.

After descending from the tower, visitors can explore the museum grounds and restored historic buildings that tell the story of the lighthouse's fascinating past. The exhibits cover the lighthouse's construction before the Civil War, a tumultuous period in American history when this beacon first began its service. The displays also detail the lighthouse's years as an active Coast Guard station, highlighting the evolution of lighthouse keeping and maritime safety over the generations. The combination of climbing the working lighthouse and exploring the museum grounds offers a comprehensive look at how this structure has served the Florida coast for more than 165 years, making it both an educational experience and a memorable visit for anyone interested in maritime history or simply seeking those spectacular views from the top of the red brick tower.

hero.headline: Linda Noskova recovers from match point collapse to win Wimbledon
hero.teaser: Linda Noskova overcame a second-set meltdown in which she wasted five match points to defeat Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final on Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy.
hero.body:
The 21-year-old Noskova recovered from a second-set meltdown in which she wasted five match points to overcome Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final on Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy. Noskova became the third Czech woman in four years to win the grass-court major, after Marketa Vondrousova in 2023 and Barbora Krejcikova in 2024. Petra Kvitova, who won Wimbledon in 2011 and 2014, was in attendance, as was Martina Navratilova, who won a record nine singles titles at the All England Club.

Navratilova looked on from the Royal Box, where she was seated next to Kate, the Princess of Wales, who was due to present the Venus Rosewater Dish trophy to Noskova. Muchova and Noskova played doubles together at the 2024 Paris Olympics and finished fourth. In the men's final on Sunday, top-ranked Jannik Sinner will attempt to defend his title against French Open champion Alexander Zverev.

cards.headline: Park Vista Community High School football team aims for state playoffs this season
cards.teaser: Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on momentum from winning four of its last five games in 2025 as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026.
cards.body:
The Cobras struggled early in 2025 but finished strong, and now the team is working to carry that success through the entire 2026 season. Senior Harris Bender said it felt good throughout the second half of last season and the team is working toward executing all year with all the pieces now in place.

The ultimate goal is the state playoffs and eventually a state title, something Park Vista has not achieved since 2017. Head football coach Donald Hanna said the team must take it one game at a time and cannot look past anyone. Senior Erik Lee said the team has the guys needed to get it done, but they must put in the work to get there. Senior Justice Jones said it will feel amazing when it happens.

Park Vista opens the 2026 season on the road against Atlantic in August.

cards.headline: US star Christian Pulisic fractured leg in World Cup loss to Belgium
cards.teaser: Christian Pulisic fractured his right leg during the Americans' World Cup loss to Belgium and will be sidelined for several weeks, a person familiar with the injury said Thursday.
cards.body:
U.S. star Christian Pulisic fractured his right leg during the Americans' World Cup loss to Belgium and will be sidelined for several weeks, a person familiar with the injury said Thursday. The person spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because the diagnosis, first reported by The Athletic, had not yet been announced by the U.S. Soccer Federation. Pulisic has a bone bruise and a microfracture of his tibia and fibula, the person said. He is expected to be able to resume training before AC Milan's Serie A opener at Torino on Aug. 23, the person added.

Pulisic hit a leg of Belgium captain Youri Tielemans while attempting a shot in the 52nd minute of Monday's 4-1 round-of-16 loss at Seattle. He remained in the game but was hobbling and Sebastian Berhalter replaced him in the 59th minute. Pulisic failed to score in the World Cup, missing one of the Americans' five matches because of a calf injury and leaving two other games early. He has 30 goals in 90 international appearances. Pulisic, who turns 28 in September, is entering his fourth season with Milan.

hero.headline: Florida families can save hundreds during 32-day back-to-school sales tax holiday starting July 20
hero.teaser: Florida's annual back-to-school sales tax holiday runs from July 20 through Aug. 20, offering 32 days of tax-free shopping on clothing, school supplies, and computers.
hero.body:
Florida families can save hundreds of dollars during the state's annual back-to-school sales tax holiday, running from July 20 through Aug. 20, 2026. The 32-day, tax-free shopping period offers no sales tax on qualifying purchases. A family spending $500 on qualifying items could save $35 in sales tax. Clothing items including shirts, pants, dresses, shoes, uniforms, and athletic wear qualify for the exemption, along with bags such as backpacks, handbags, diaper bags and fanny packs, and accessories including wallets, belts, ties, and graduation caps and gowns. Notable exclusions include briefcases, suitcases, watches, jewelry, skis, swim fins, roller blades and any clothing item over $100. Tax-free school supplies include pens, pencils, erasers, crayons, notebooks, binders, folders, construction paper, poster board, markers, scissors, glue, tape, staplers, lunch boxes, composition books, and blank CDs. Learning aids such as flashcards, learning cards, jigsaw puzzles, puzzle books, interactive books, educational toys, memory and matching games, stacking blocks and educational sets also qualify.

Qualifying computers include laptops, desktops, tablets, electronic book readers, and calculators, along with accessories such as keyboards, mice, monitors without TV tuners, printers, ink cartridges, modems, routers, cables, educational and productivity software, storage devices and memory cards. Computers must be for personal, non-commercial use. Items must meet specific price thresholds: clothing and bags $100 or less per item, school supplies $50 or less, learning aids and puzzles $30 or less, and computers and accessories $1,500 or less. Items normally sold together must be purchased as a set and cannot be split up to meet price thresholds. The exemption is not available at theme parks and entertainment complexes, hotels and public lodging establishments, or airports. Items ordered online during the holiday period qualify even if delivered after Aug. 20. Florida retailers have no option to opt out of the sales tax holiday and must process all qualifying purchases tax-free during the designated period.

cards.teaser: Florida's home insurance market is showing signs of improvement with more insurers returning and some rates declining.
cards.body: The improvement in Florida's home insurance market represents a shift after years of insurers leaving the state or raising rates. The return of additional insurers to the Florida market could provide homeowners with more coverage options. Some homeowners are seeing rate declines, though the extent of rate reductions varies by insurer and location across the state.

hero.headline: Aldi opens in Hobe Sound as Treasure Coast shoppers seek relief from rising grocery costs
hero.teaser: A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, bringing more affordable choices to customers already facing tight budgets. The opening comes
hero.body:
A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, bringing more affordable choices to customers already facing tight budgets. The opening comes as the USDA expects grocery prices to rise 2.8% this year, prompting more households to adjust their purchasing decisions based on price rather than preference. For shoppers looking to stretch their dollars, the discount grocer offers an alternative to traditional supermarkets at a time when food costs continue to climb.

Customers Cheryl and Tony Cooperman said they are excited an affordable option like the new Aldi store is now open close to their home. Cheryl said grocery prices are getting expensive and are starting to change the way she shops. "They're the type of people who never used to look at prices, but now she will go with what's on sale instead of just with what they want, and they never used to do that," she said. The changing shopping habits reflect a broader trend as more households look for ways to manage rising food costs.

Price movements in key grocery categories show a mixed picture for consumers. Egg prices are dropping, and beef prices fell 1.3% from April to May, though wholesale beef prices remain at all-time highs for this time of year. Pork rose 1% from April to May, and chicken prices rose 1.3% over the same period. Fruits and vegetables are seeing an increase of less than 1%. Despite some declining categories, the overall trajectory points to continued upward pressure on grocery bills.

Shoppers James and Harry said Thursday they do not expect relief at the register anytime soon. "Prices are gonna stay inflated and are not gonna go down," they said, adding they would be willing to bet on that. Still, they said stores like Aldi, which often have lower prices than other stores, can make a difference for everyday shoppers. "Having stuff like this for the average person is extremely beneficial because there's nobody who isn't feeling the price increase," they said. The new location gives Treasure Coast residents another option for managing household budgets as inflation continues to impact the cost of food.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast Traffic Report: Major Ramp and Road Closures Planned July 12-17

hero.body:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

Drivers across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 10-17 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department of Transportation's latest weekly traffic report identifies multiple lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties. FDOT placed additional emphasis on full road, ramp and bridge closures expected to have the greatest effect on motorists.

## Major closures to know about

### I-95 exit to Bridge Road closing overnight in Martin County

The southbound Interstate 95 exit ramp to County Road 708, also known as Bridge Road, at Exit 96 will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16.**

Drivers will be directed to exit at Kanner Highway, travel south on Pratt Whitney Road and then head east on Bridge Road.

The closure is needed for roadway construction. Weather-related contingency dates are scheduled for July 19-23.

### Port St. Lucie neighborhood roads could close for several days

Extended closures are planned along several side streets near the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project.

Closures may begin at **7 a.m. Monday, July 13, and continue until 5 p.m. Friday, July 17,** on portions of SW Jaslo Avenue, SW Jacoby Avenue, SW McCullough Avenue, SW McCall Road and SW McHord Avenue.

The roads will close intermittently for drainage and utility installation. FDOT said adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained.

Detours will generally use SW Paar Drive, SW McCain Street, SW McIntyre Street, SW Kabane Street and other nearby roads, depending on the closure location.

### I-95 ramp to Orange Avenue closing in Fort Pierce

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to westbound State Road 68, or Orange Avenue, will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16.**

Motorists will be detoured using the exit to eastbound Orange Avenue, northbound Jenkins Road and westbound Loop Road before returning to westbound Orange Avenue.

The work includes paving and lighting installation. Contingency dates are July 19-23.

## Martin County traffic impacts

Motorists should expect overnight lane closures on I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line. Up to two lanes may close in each direction during overnight hours for milling, resurfacing and signage work.

On U.S. 1 in Stuart, two lanes may close intermittently between Fischer Street and Decker Avenue from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday for sign installation.

A1A between Shore Village Terrace and the Jensen Beach Causeway may be reduced to one lane at times from Monday through Friday for drainage work and pavement widening. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic through the work zone.

Martin Highway between Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard may also have intermittent overnight lane closures Tuesday through Thursday.

FDOT is additionally warning drivers in advance about several upcoming I-95 ramp closures at Martin Highway and Kanner Highway later in July and early August.

## St. Lucie County traffic impacts

Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Seafury Lane and Lennard Road may have daytime lane closures Monday through Friday. Two lanes may close overnight from Sunday through Friday for drainage work, milling and repaving.

U.S. 1 between Jennings Road and Golden Oak Trail may also have lane restrictions during both daytime and overnight hours.

On SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard, one lane may close between Jordin Avenue and Alcantarra Boulevard from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday as crews continue the widening project.

Up to two lanes may close overnight on I-95 between Glades Cut-Off Road and the area just south of Okeechobee Road for milling and repaving.

Midway Road between Florida's Turnpike and Selvitz Road may continue to have intermittent weekday lane closures through September as part of the roadway widening project.

## North Causeway marine restrictions

The new A1A North Causeway Bridge remains open to vehicle traffic, but significant restrictions are planned for boaters using the Intracoastal Waterway.

The existing drawbridge will not open to marine traffic from 7 a.m. Thursday, July 16, through 6 p.m. Saturday, July 18. Boats capable of passing beneath the bridge without an opening may continue through.

Additional single-leaf openings, partial channel obstructions and temporary full channel closures are scheduled through July 24 as crews remove portions of the former drawbridge.

FDOT said the marine work will not affect vehicle traffic on the new bridge.

## Indian River County traffic impacts

One lane may remain closed on the 17th Street bridges between Indian River Boulevard and Indian Bay Drive as bridge rehabilitation continues.

At the new I-95 interchange at Oslo Road, one or two interstate lanes may close overnight Sunday through Thursday for bridge work, milling and resurfacing.

On 90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street, one lane may close overnight Sunday through Friday for construction associated with the 85th Street widening project.

Drivers traveling near Sebastian Inlet should also expect intermittent lane or shoulder closures on A1A through Friday, July 17. Flaggers will direct motorists through the work zone.

Sections of the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park will remain closed during construction of the new bridge. The closures are expected to continue through spring 2032, although the park and portions of both parking lots remain open.

## Plan ahead

Construction schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions. Motorists should allow additional travel time, follow posted detours and use caution around workers and equipment.

Real-time interstate traffic conditions are available through Florida 511. Updated lane closure information is also available through FDOT District Four.
